title: Finite monoid-ideal generators and a minimal exponent outside a smaller ideal
statement:
Let $P$ be a commutative additive monoid with identity $0$, generated by finitely many elements, integral (its canonical map into its group completion [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] is injective), hence cancellative (that is, $x+z=y+z$ implies $x=y$), and sharp (that is, $x+y=0$ implies $x=y=0$). A monoid ideal is a subset $I\subseteq P$ with $I+P\subseteq I$, and the empty subset is allowed. For every monoid ideal $K$ there is a finite subset $S\subseteq K$ such that $K=\bigcup_{s\in S}(s+P)$. If $J\subsetneq K$ is another monoid ideal, one can choose such an $S$ and $p\in S\setminus J$ with
$$p\notin K+P^+,\qquad P^+=P\setminus\{0\},\quad K+P^+=\{k+q:k\in K,\ q\in P^+\}.$$
Thus $p=k+q$, $k\in K$, forces $q=0$ and $k=p$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110 (PDF p. 116), the sentence asserting that the sharp monoid residue ring is a quotient of the monomial-ideal quotient; Proof (1)--(2) ancestry of lem-trf-local-term-locality, through the nearby-duality alteration chain and Expose VIII 3.4.3: the finite-generation and minimal-exponent argument in old step 3 of the monoidal-ideal contraction proof.

proof.text: Choose generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $P$ and put $\phi:\mathbf N^d\to P$, $\phi(a)=\sum_i a_i g_i$. This is a surjective additive map by finite generation, including $d=0$. Put $U=\phi^{-1}(K)$. If $a\in U$ and $b\ge a$ coordinatewise, then $b=a+c$ for $c\in\mathbf N^d$, so $\phi(b)=\phi(a)+\phi(c)\in K$. Thus $U$ is upward closed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110 (PDF p. 116), implicit finite-generation/minimal-exponent justification of the monomial quotient. Agent-supplied details using Dickson minimal domination.

proof.text: Let $B=\{b\in U:\ \forall c\in U,\ c\le b\Rightarrow c=b\}$. Distinct elements of $B$ are incomparable: for $b,b'\in B$, $b\le b'$ and minimality of $b'$ force $b=b'$. Hence $B$ is finite by the antichain clause of [lem-trf-monomial-upper-set-finite-basis]. Its minimal-domination clause also gives, for every $a\in U$, some $b\in B$ with $b\le a$. Both clauses apply to the arbitrary subset $U\subseteq\mathbf N^d$ without further hypotheses. If $U$ is empty, $B$ is empty.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110 (PDF p. 116), implicit finite-generation/minimal-exponent justification of the monomial quotient. Agent-supplied details using Dickson minimal domination.

proof.text: Put $T=\phi(B)\subseteq K$; it is finite. For $k\in K$, choose $a\in\mathbf N^d$ with $\phi(a)=k$ and then $b\in B$ below $a$ by Step 2. Coordinatewise subtraction gives $a=b+c$ with $c\in\mathbf N^d$, so $k=\phi(b)+\phi(c)\in\phi(b)+P$. Conversely every $t+P$, $t\in T$, lies in $K$ by the ideal condition. Therefore $K=\bigcup_{t\in T}(t+P)$; for $K=\varnothing$ this says $T=\varnothing$ generates it.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110 (PDF p. 116), implicit finite-generation/minimal-exponent justification of the monomial quotient. Agent-supplied details using Dickson minimal domination.

proof.text: The subsets of finite $T$ generating $K$ form a finite nonempty family, since $T$ generates $K$. Choose a member $S$ of least cardinality. Suppose $s\in S$ and $s=k+q$ with $k\in K$ and $q\in P^+$. Write $k=t+r$ with $t\in S$ and $r\in P$. If $t=s$, cancellation in $s=s+(r+q)$ gives $r+q=0$, and sharpness gives $q=0$, contradicting $q\in P^+$. If $t\ne s$, every $s+v$, $v\in P$, equals $t+(r+q+v)$, where $r+q+v\in P$. Thus $S\setminus\{s\}$ still generates $K$ and has smaller cardinality, again a contradiction. Hence every $s\in S$ lies outside $K+P^+$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, printed p. 110 (PDF p. 116), implicit finite-generation/minimal-exponent justification of the monomial quotient. Agent-supplied details using Dickson minimal domination.

proof.text: If $J\subsetneq K$, choose $k_0\in K\setminus J$. By generation write $k_0=p+r$ with $p\in S$ and $r\in P$. If $p\in J$, the ideal condition gives $k_0=p+r\in J$, a contradiction; hence $p\in S\setminus J$. Step 4 gives $p\notin K+P^+$. Finally $p=k+q$ with $k\in K$, $q\in P$ forces $q=0$ by this exclusion, and then $k=p$. This $S$ and $p$ satisfy every requested clause.

split_report.summary: Pull the ideal back along a finite generating map from N^d; reuse the existing Dickson minimal-domination/antichain Mathlib leaf to obtain finitely many generators. Choose a generating subset of least cardinality and prove its generators lie outside K+P^+ by cancellation, sharpness, and an explicit redundancy calculation. Strict inclusion supplies a generator outside J. No new nodes or statement changes. Rechecked the current group-completion definition, both clauses of the current Dickson leaf, the ILO source, and the empty, zero-dimensional, nonfree, nonsaturated and torsion group-completion cases.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q116-e2885e247 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all five proof steps in full. This is the fourth delivery of the same split, with 0 new nodes and the statement and stmt_deps unchanged. Compared with the snapshot of the previous head 6c09542cc79, only steps 2 and 4 and the split_report differ, and only in wording: step 4 now assumes q in P^+ from the start and ends both cases in a contradiction. No re-split repair note exists for this item. I checked each step. Step 1: the map from N^d is surjective by finite generation, and the preimage U of K is closed upward. Step 2: the minimal elements B of U form an antichain, and both clauses of lem-trf-monomial-upper-set-finite-basis apply exactly, for any subset and also for d=0. Step 3: K is generated by phi(B), and K empty gives an empty set. Step 4: take S as a generating subset of least cardinality. The case t=s gives a contradiction by cancellation and sharpness. The case t≠s gives s+v=t+(r+q+v), so S minus s still generates K, contradicting minimality. Step 5: k0 in K\J gives p in S\J, and p lies outside K+P^+. I tested the statement on these cases: the zero monoid with K empty, and with K=P and J empty; N with K=2+N and J=3+N; N^2; the monoid generated by 2 and 3; and the monoid generated by (1,0) and (1,1) in ZxZ/2. I checked ILO Exposé VIII Lemma 3.4.3 on PDF p.116: it uses the monomial quotient without justifying it, and the proof is correctly marked as agent-written. No SGA source is used. A whole-DAG rg -L search found no duplicate node. The citer lem-trf-log-regular-monoidal-ideal-contraction uses the statement as it stands. No fixes were needed.
